newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- mostly unchanged, quiet.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- mostly unchanged, quiet.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were mostly unchanged in quiet midday action Thursday, as traders said the market appeared to be resting from gains earlier in the week.
"I think everyone's kind of digesting what happened during the course of the week," one trader said. "Muni prices are staying firm from yesterday."

A second trader said he was awaiting the free-to-trade announcement on Wednesday's $265 million Washington general obligation offering. He said the deal did not appear to be well-placed, and he expected some price concessions when the bonds begin changing hands.

J.P. Morgan Securities Inc. tentatively priced Thursday's largest negotiated offering, a $399 million Municipal Electric Authority of Georgia deal. The issue came at a top yield of 5.48 percent in 2020.

Goldman, Sachs & Co. won the day's largest competitive offering, a $40 million Kansas City, Mo., general obligation deal. The firm reoffered the 2017 term bonds at a 5.25 percent yield, and said later in the day it had an $11 million balance.
Treasury prices initially firmed Wednesday after the Labor Department found an unexpected surge in jobless claims, which jumped to 377,000 in the week ended July 5 from 337,000 a week earlier.
But the market retreated after economists said the figure was not a sign of a weakening economy, but instead reflected expected shutdowns at car-makers as they retool to make new models.
The government long bond was off 5/32 at 100-20/32 to yield 6.58 percent.

Friday's Producer Price Index for June is the next major data focus for the market. Forecast call for the figure to be unchanged overall and up 0.1 percent excluding food and energy, according to a Reuters consensus survey of economists.
In the secondary market for municipal bonds, bids on Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania and New Jersey FGIC 5-1/2s of 2026 were unchanged from Wednesday at 100.
Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority FGIC 5.0s of 2027 were bid at 5.42 percent, down one basis point.
Municipal futures for September fell 5/32 to 119-6/32, while September Treasury bond futures lost 7/32 to 113-22/32. The MOB spread widened to 176 ticks from 174 at the close on Wednesday.
